business_impact: Customs-related messages unable to send or receive in IT, IE, CH, ES regions, affecting cross-border operations and causing delays for multiple customers
affected_customers: Multiple customers in EMEA region with active customs document workflows
estimated_customer_impact: Approximately 50,000 messages in backlog; 8-10 customers with delayed deliveries
root_cause: A database routine shared by several integration processes had been configured with database settings optimized for only one of them. The other processes experienced performance degradation, resulting in a message processing backlog.

timeline_events.description: Incident declared - Customs message delivery failures reported in IT region by support team
Database Performance Team begins analysis; identifies higher-than-normal query times in customs processing routine
Root cause identified - database routine configuration query optimizer settings don't match current workload profile
Customs Integration Team confirms: configuration issue affecting all calling processes except the one it was originally tuned for
Temporary mitigation applied - affected database routine restarted with default configuration; processes restarted
Message queue began clearing; monitoring throughput recovery
Service restored - message backlog cleared; all queued customs messages processing normally
Incident declared resolved; teams standing down from war room
Customer communication sent to all affected accounts describing incident, impact, and resolution
Database Performance Team begins detailed analysis of permanent configuration fix

immediate_fix: Restarted the database routine and all affected integration processes with default configuration. This immediately restored the routine's performance to normal levels. The message queue began clearing within 5 minutes, and all approximately 50,000 queued messages were processed within 45 minutes.
permanent_fix: Implement process-specific configuration profiles for the database routine, with pre-deployment configuration validation rules to prevent similar misconfiguration. Expected completion: 30 November. Currently in progress with Database Performance Team.

prevention_measures.action: Implement pre-deployment configuration validation checks for all database routines
prevention_measures.target: Prevents misconfiguration from being deployed to production

prevention_measures.action: Add automated monitoring and alerting for database routine performance degradation
prevention_measures.target: Detects similar issues earlier; alerts on performance deviation

prevention_measures.action: Create detailed runbook documenting database routine configuration requirements for each calling process
prevention_measures.target: Ensures future configuration changes include proper process-specific tuning

prevention_measures.action: Add configuration review step to change management process for database routine modifications
prevention_measures.target: Creates checkpoint to catch configuration issues before production impact

customer_communication_details.content_summary: Detailed incident description, timeline, impact summary, and resolution confirmation

notes:
This incident highlighted the critical importance of process-specific database performance tuning. The database routine had been optimized during initial implementation for one calling process, but as new integration processes were added over time, the original configuration became suboptimal for them. This underscores the need for more systematic configuration management and validation.

All affected customers in the IT (Italy), IE (Ireland), CH (Switzerland), and ES (Spain) regions were notified. Customer feedback during follow-up was positive regarding the rapid response and clear communication.

post_incident_actions_outstanding.action: Update change management process to include configuration validation step
